transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-17
Start: 08:42 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Kai (Redwood CSM), Priya (Gallium Head of ML), Marcus (Gallium Data), Ellen (Gallium PM), Jordan (Gallium SRE), Samira (Gallium Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on fidelity/regression checks for the pilot prompt set; ran through recent failures from the scorecard, tuned a few prompts live, agreed to run a 24-hour latency/cost benchmark, and to rehearse a rollback in staging. Security clarifications around KMS and SSO were requested.

Topics covered:
- Recent regression spike (scorecard slices)
- Prompt-set pruning & synthetic negative cases
- Thresholds for automatic fallback to smaller model variant
- Canary/rollback playbook and staging drill
- Security: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention
- Next steps and owners

Partial action items (also in metadata above): see action_items list

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alyssa: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: Priya here, and Marcus, Ellen, Jordan, Samira on from Gallium.
[00:10] Alyssa: great, Devon i'll hand off to you to run the fidelity summary?
[00:15] Devon: yeah sure — so we pulled the last scorecard overnight, we saw a bump in false positives on the financial-extraction slice, about a 7% uptick week over last. Most of those are prompt-edge cases where the model hallucinated dates or amounts. there's a sample in the scorecard spreadsheet, note the cell refs are a bit off sometimes because of my export.
[00:41] Priya: can you remind me which model variant we ran against for that card? was it quantized-v2 or the fp16 baseline?
[00:46] Devon: it was quant-v2 with the token-cache enabled — we wanted the lower cost path but that may be interacting with the prompt prefixes. also we saw slightly higher latency tail at 99th pct during bursts.
[01:05] Marcus: that 99th tail — is that infra (network) or model? our SLO is 200ms p99. you said it was close?
[01:12] Devon: it's mostly model-side, the KV cache warm/cold transitions add a bit of jitter for long contexts; network added maybe ~10ms occasionally. we can change routing to a dedicated pool to stabilize.
[01:24] Ellen: from product POV, the key is fidelity not micro-latency, we can tolerate 20ms variance if it improves accuracy.
[01:30] Alyssa: good note. Kai, did you pull the prompt diff for the financial extraction set?
[01:36] Kai: yes, i pushed a curated 200-case set to the folder and flagged 18 prompts that are brittle. link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/gallium-promptset
[01:46] Priya: thanks, i'll upload labels for those 200 cases today. the acceptance threshold we discussed is 92% F1 for extraction.
[01:54] Devon: okay, so plan A: apply small prompt surgery — add clarifying tokens and stricter delimiters — and re-run scoring. Plan B: if that fails, auto-fallback to smaller but more deterministic variant for the extraction endpoint.
[02:05] Jordan: quick Q on fallback — will that change customer routing? we have a multi-tenant staging and want to ensure isolation.
[02:12] Devon: fallback will be per-route and per-model policy, so it won't spill over tenants; Redwood supports pinning and route-level policies. there might be a short restart for the model instance but we can mitigate with warm replicas.
[02:25] Samira: security question: what happens to KV cache and any cached prefixes — are those encrypted at rest? and if we run Dedicated/Private, can we bring our KMS?
[02:34] Alyssa: yes, cache data is stored encrypted. for Private deployments you can bring your own key (KMS/HSM) and Redwood integrates with AWS KMS and Vault, we have a doc: https://redwood.com/security/kms-integration.pdf
[02:48] Samira: do you have SOC2 evidence and penetration-testing summaries?
[02:52] Alyssa: we do; i'll post the SOC2 and pentest summary in the CRM. short answer: SOC2 Type II in 2025, and quarterly pentest cadence.
[03:02] Priya: wonder if we can simulate adversarial prompts as part of the guardrail test? we saw one case where prompt-injection caused attribute overwrite.
[03:12] Devon: yes, we recommend adding synthetic adversarial examples to the evaluation set; Kai, can you add a 40-case adversarial set?
[03:18] Kai: yep, i'll add that this afternoon.
[03:22] Ellen: on scoring, the recent regression correlated to a model patch we pulled last week — is rollback immediate? what's the playbook?
[03:30] Devon: we have an automatic rollback policy that can revert to previous model commit if the scorecard diverges beyond threshold. it uses per-route health checks, and we can run a dry-run in staging where the rollback is exercised without flipping prod traffic — that's what we'd like to rehearse.
[03:44] Jordan: perfect — we'll schedule the staging dry-run. question: will the rollback preserve ongoing KV caches? we don't want to invalidate warm caches and cause a big warm-up penalty.
[03:53] Devon: good point — rollback will start a new model instance, so caches are per-instance; we recommend a staged rollout with warm replicas to reduce cold-starts. Jordan, you can pin warm instances in staging for the drill.
[04:05] Priya: can you also add a smoke test that checks extraction F1 on a holdout set post-rollback?
[04:12] Devon: yes, smoke test will run the holdout 200 cases and compare to acceptance threshold.
[04:16] Marcus: can the smoke test run within the same minute-level window as the rollback? we need to prove non-regression quickly.
[04:22] Devon: yes, smoke runs parallel and returns pass/fail within the pipeline.
[04:25] Alyssa: switching gears — cost control: we want to cap spend for the pilot. Marcus, can you remind us of the cap?
[04:31] Marcus: we're capping at $25k/mo for the pilot in staging, we'd like Redwood to recommend batching/quantization settings to fit.
[04:38] Alyssa: we'll run a constrained benchmark and produce recommended settings: batching, sequence-length caps, and quant profile.
[04:44] Devon: note that some quant profiles reduce hallucination robustness, so we'll trade off in the recommendation and show delta on the scorecard.
[04:52] Priya: important: any PII touched by the model path — what's redact/retention policy?
[04:57] Alyssa: Redwood's hosted option can be configured to not persist inputs, but for explicit retention we can set TTLs and have audit logs sent to your sink. for regulated data, Private is recommended.
[05:08] Samira: ok please send a short matrix — hosted vs dedicated vs private with retention and compliance tradeoffs.
[05:13] Alyssa: will do.
[05:16] Devon: back to the scorecard, i'll walk through two live examples — case A and case B — i'll share my screen — (screen share noise)
[05:30] [screen pause] Speaker 1: (mumbling) the first example shows the model adding a date that wasn't there, see example row 42.
[05:39] Devon: yep, row 42 — prompt includes an ambiguous phrase 'last payment' — clarifying to 'last payment date (MM-DD-YYYY)' reduces ambiguity. we'll push that edit.
[05:47] Priya: can we automate a transformation that adds delimiters for numeric extraction?
[05:51] Devon: yes, we can add a preprocessor or instruct the model with a stronger system prompt. tradeoffs: preprocess is deterministic but requires pipeline change; prompt fix is faster.
[06:02] Ellen: do prompt transforms affect other routes? we only want to change extraction route.
[06:07] Devon: correct — route-level prompts are supported.
[06:10] Priya: curious about latency impact of preprocessing — any numbers?
[06:14] Devon: generally <10ms, depends on transform complexity.
[06:18] Marcus: ok.
[06:20] Alyssa: last big item: can we get a 24-hour benchmark run with real traffic profile? Marcus you'll share traffic histogram?
[06:27] Marcus: yes, i'll export the traffic trace and drop into the shared folder.
[06:30] Devon: i'll schedule the run and share the results with raw logs and scorecard, target finish by Friday.
[06:36] Priya: great.
[06:38] [10 minute pass — mid call edit notes omitted for brevity]
[16:38] Jordan: rehearsal details — we propose doing the staging rollback at 02:00 PST next week, with a 30-minute window for the drill, then validate with smoke tests.
[16:46] Alyssa: confirmed we can support that window. we'll provide a runbook snapshot.
[16:52] Samira: security will want to observe and maybe run a quick auth scan during the exercise.
[16:56] Kai: noted — i'll add a checklist to the runbook.
[17:00] Priya: one more ask — can we get per-prompt difficulty heatmap? that helped us triage previously.
[17:05] Devon: yes, we'll deliver a heatmap showing prompt failure rates, confidence, and latency per-case.
[17:10] Ellen: also request: example-level diffs pre/post-prompt-surgery so product can sign off.
[17:15] Devon: can do.
[17:18] Alyssa: okay wrapping — recap of owners and dates — Devon will run 24h perf (due 2026-02-20), Kai will add adversarial set and update promptset (due 2026-02-18), Alyssa to send security pack (due 2026-02-18), Jordan to allocate staging nodes and confirm rollback hooks (due 2026-02-21), Priya to upload labelled cases (due 2026-02-18).
[17:40] Priya: that works for us.
[17:43] Marcus: quick note — we're evaluating VertexAI too for a separate use case, but primary is throughput vs fidelity here.
[17:50] Alyssa: understood; we'll make sure the benchmarking includes comparable configs.
[17:54] Kai: final, i'll schedule the next check-in for 2026-02-24 same time.
[17:59] Ellen: thanks everyone.
[18:02] Alyssa: thanks, we'll follow up in CRM with artifacts. bye.

End of transcript.
